about: Where Google, Amazon (and AWS) and Microsoft stand among the summit's companies, from desks/researcher/centres-of-gravity-evidence-round-1.md (researcher@PrompTugal.dinis, read 6 November 2026, public pages only). Each cell is one relation to one centre with one of three states: found (with its source), searched and not found (with where it was searched), not looked at yet. A list read in full is dated: it changes before the summit. By dev.graphs@PrompTugal.dinis.

builton.text: Of the 14 partner companies' pages read, three name Google Cloud: Elastic (on its cloud marketplace), Datadog (a monitoring product page; no partnership claimed) and ManageEngine (cloud security for Azure, AWS and GCP as a product area; coverage, not a partnership). A page not showing something does not mean the tie is absent. A menu link, a customer story or a rival comparison is not a partnership, and each line says which it is.

builton.label: 11 of 17 sell on AWS Marketplace
builton.text: Two lenses. Front pages (14 of the 17 other partner companies read): five name AWS, in different ways: Cerebras (a testimonial by an AWS vice president on a joint inference setup, not called a partnership), Elastic (on its cloud marketplace), Datadog (a monitoring product page, no partnership claimed), ManageEngine (product coverage) and Runpod (a customer compares AWS as the more expensive rival). AWS Marketplace search by company name (all 17, first results only): 11 have a listing of their own, nine under their own name (1Password, Akamai, Cerebras, Datadog, Elastic, IBM, Runpod, Twilio, VTEX) and two under a parent (Cisco for Cisco Outshift, Zoho for ManageEngine); several hold an AWS Specialization badge. A listing shows the company sells there; it is not a stated partnership. A front page understates the tie (Twilio and VTEX said nothing on theirs yet both sell there), so the marketplace is the better first source. Not found in the first results: Mozilla, Gcore, Genspark, KPMG and PitchBook, and the search is fuzzy, so that is not proof of none. Delinea appears only through resellers. The Google Cloud and Microsoft marketplaces could not be read (one shows nothing without interaction, the other refuses automated readers), so only AWS has a marketplace lens.

past.text: Microsoft is shown under "Some partners from our past events" on Web Summit's partners page; the edition is not given, and no 2026 listing was found. The organiser's own 2024 and 2025 takeaway posts name the partners exhibiting; neither list names AWS, Google or Microsoft (2025 names Alibaba Cloud), so the 2022 naming did not repeat in those lists. Those lists are short and mid-event, so this is not absence. Separately, Start Campus, the operator of the Sines data centre campus, reported on 11 November 2025 an announcement by Microsoft of USD 10 billion for that campus, after remarks by Microsoft's president at the opening of Web Summit Lisbon: Microsoft's largest Portugal announcement, made in Web Summit week. Portugal's trade agency AICEP also records it (Portugalglobal, 11 December 2025). Microsoft's own page was not read, and he is not on the organiser's listed line-up for that opening night, so he is not described here as a listed speaker; no stage or time is given. Nscale's releases (15 October 2025, 5 May 2026) describe the deliveries to Microsoft at that campus; its own spending is a different figure from Microsoft's USD 10 billion. The relation is 'announced at the summit's opening': neither partner, exhibitor nor speaker's employer in the lists.
